propositions: The primary watcher (mirror-guard.yml workflow) evaluates replication health on a single instantaneous fetch, triggering false-positive alarms during expected post-submit Gerrit→GitHub lag (~15s) that self-heals within minutes.

The module's design docstring (shipped in d96628c9dca) and secondary CloudWatch alarm both implement sustained-divergence windows for lag absorption; the primary watcher's single-sample behavior contradicts this designed absorption and was never wired in (incomplete-implementation).

The fix adds an in-process, portable evaluation window (3 samples × 45s spacing, tunable via CLI flags) to run() and main() that returns healthy when divergence converges within the window, while preserving failures for persistent or GitHub-ahead divergence.

Convergence on any sample within the window returns exit 0 with a reason noting transient lag; persistent divergence returns exit 1 with a 'stalled' reason or sample count; missing SHAs fail immediately without re-sampling (no weakening: today's failure set minus lag-that-converges).

The fix is scheduler-agnostic and portable—the tolerance lives in the module, not in CI provider state or retry machinery—and was validated with 5 new behavioral unit tests (transient-converges, persistent-static, moving-never-converging, in-sync cost, missing-SHA immediate).
Defect origin: a774-5ca9-3a80-4f6d (scope-of-work); the omission shipped with a774's own introducing commit d96628c9dca and was never broken by later changes.
